narrative.overview: EasyPhysio should feel like a well-kept patient file that happens to be software — not a generic SaaS dashboard wearing a healthcare skin. The system runs two coordinated registers rather than one flat palette: a cooler slate register for marketing/acquisition surfaces that reads as a confident, credible B2B tool, and a warmer stone/paper register for the actual clinical work that reads as considered and human. Both share the same type pairing, radius language, and blue brand accent, so the app never feels like two different products — only two moods for two different jobs.
keyCharacteristics: Warm display serif for headings, humanist sans for everything else — never a system-default stack.
Two-register neutral system: cool slate for marketing, warm stone/paper for clinical work.
Generous, consistent rounding (never sharp corners) — pill buttons, xl–3xl cards.
Mostly flat cards that lift only on hover with soft, colored, directional shadows — never ambient drop-shadows at rest.
Left-accent-border cards for triage/alert rows instead of full-color alert boxes.
Motion is calm and purposeful, never decorative.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Marketing and acquisition surfaces use the slate neutral scale; the dashboard and anything inside a patient's actual record use stone/paper. Never mix the two on the same surface.

rules.name: The Sparse Accent Rule
rules.body: Brand blue marks the one primary action or highlight on a screen — never decorative.

rules.name: The Display-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: font-display (Fraunces) is reserved for headings only — body copy, labels, and UI chrome always stay on the sans stack.

rules.name: The Earned-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow appears because of interaction (hover) or because an element is the single most important action on the screen — never as ambient decoration on a resting card.

dos: Do keep the slate/stone register split intentional.
Do use font-display (Fraunces) for headings only.
Do let shadows appear only on hover or on the single primary action of a screen.
Do use the 3px left-accent-border pattern for triage/alert cards.
Do keep motion calm: staggered fade-ins, no bounce, no spin, pulse reserved for genuinely urgent state.
donts: Don't use emoji as UI icons — lucide-react only.
Don't introduce a third neutral scale alongside slate and stone.
Don't apply ambient/always-on shadows to resting cards.
Don't let the app read as generic AI SaaS: no purple gradient heroes, no default system-font stacks, no stock dashboard-template layouts.
